name: Atmospheric Imaging Radar

velocity.reason: 2013 AIR velocity not validated; published instrument limitations
velocity.detail: Kurdzo et al. (2017), p. 918 and Table 2, report technical difficulties and do not present radial velocity before 2014. The later archive contains VEL, but provides no verified correction or validation history. Those values are retained only for audit, not displayed as usable winds.

geolocation.note: Rendered directly from archived radar location, true-north azimuth and range. An independent comparison flags several-kilometer disagreement between a first-frame circulation feature and the contemporaneous NWS track; the source of that discrepancy is unresolved. Do not use AIR pixels for a precise tornado position or chase-distance estimate.

attribution: Atmospheric Imaging Radar data provided by the Advanced Radar Research Center, University of Oklahoma. Derived visualization; see source publications and archive terms.

sources.title: OU ARRC curated radar archive and data policy
AIR El Reno CF/Radial archive (7 GB; partial range retrieval used)
Isom et al. (2013), Atmospheric Imaging Radar system
Kurdzo et al. (2017), AIR severe-storm observations

processing.sampling: Nearest native polar gate on a Web Mercator pixel grid; no smoothing or temporal interpolation. Pixels outside native sector/range or missing gates are transparent.
processing.geometry: Spherical azimuthal-equidistant surface distance/azimuth; inverse standard 4/3-Earth beam geometry includes the recorded radar altitude. Actual range coordinate vector used, despite conflicting first-gate attribute.
processing.time: Global coverage midpoint, with full start/end preserved. Source per-ray times are zero with malformed units; no reliable individual ray acquisition time is available.
processing.velocity: Kurdzo et al. (2017), p. 918 and Table 2, report technical difficulties and do not present radial velocity before 2014. The later archive contains VEL, but provides no verified correction or validation history. Those values are retained only for audit, not displayed as usable winds.
processing.quality: Limited archive quality control and calibration information; source geolocation registration unverified. No independent calibration or additional clutter/attenuation filtering applied. Radar measurements are above ground, not a surface tornado boundary.
processing.resolution: 30 m sampled range-gate spacing; the source publication lists 45 m independent range resolution for 2013. About 0.5 degree azimuth sampling and roughly 60 m raster pixels do not establish independent 60 m spatial resolution. Radar beam footprint grows with range.
